 League of Legends: New Dawn Will Keep Every Champion and Skin, Riot Says 
 by Brett Holland on November 16, 2026 
 Every League of Legends champion and skin available today can still be used after New Dawn, the game’s sweeping overhaul, arrives later in 2027. Andrei “Meddler” van Roon, who leads League Studio at Riot Games , confirmed the point in a post on X on Nov. 15, describing New Dawn as a huge update to the current game, not a sequel and not a separate release.
 His clarification arrived a day after Riot premiered a teaser, roughly two minutes long, at the Worlds 2026 final in Brooklyn’s Barclays Center on Nov. 14. Early January 2027 is when the company will hold a complete reveal, while the launch itself still has no firm date.
 Runes are staying as well. Players will still pick them before each match, Keystone included, though van Roon explained that the system is being trimmed back to make space for other additions. Those pre-match selections change how a champion behaves in a game, with the Keystone serving as the headline choice.
 On the technical side, New Dawn runs on an improved build of Hextech, the in-house engine League has relied on since launch. Switching engines was ruled out entirely, the studio head added.
 New Dawn is also only the label for this update, he noted, and won’t be attached to the game’s name for good. Further detail has to wait for the January showcase, which van Roon wrote will cover everything in far more depth, and nearly 700 replies had built up under his thread by Nov. 16.
 Hey all,
It’s been great reading all the conversations about the New Dawn teaser from yesterday. We’ll be doing a full reveal of New Dawn in early January with a lot more detail on everything, so I can’t share too much more yet. There are some things I’ve seen crop up a lot though that I can clarify:
1 – You’ll still pick Runes, including a Keystone, in New Dawn. The Rune system is getting streamlined somewhat given other additions, it’s not getting removed though
2 – New Dawn is being built on an upgraded version of Hextech engine, the custom engine League has always used. We’re not changing to a different engine
3 – New Dawn is not a separate, stand alone game, but a massive update to League. We’re using the name “New Dawn” to refer to the update, not as a permanent addition to League’s name
4 – All current champs and skins will still be useable once New Dawn launches
— Andrei van Roon (@RiotMeddler) November 16, 2026 
 Riot slotted the teaser between the second and third games of the final, right after Bilibili Gaming edged Gen.G over 53 minutes in game two, the tournament’s longest, to level things at 1-1. Bilibili Gaming went on to clinch the world title 3-1.
 Van Roon shares the video with Paul “Pabro” Bellezza, League’s executive producer, and the pair walk through a modern client arriving in 2027, a visual rebuild of Summoner’s Rift, gameplay changes on the map and new approaches to champions players already know. “We want League to stand the test of time,” van Roon says early in the clip, before Bellezza adds that “the client, for one, has to be better.”
 Gameplay footage in the teaser shows redesigned minions, a Red Brambleback in a volcanic-looking camp and a wall beside it blasted open into a new path. Baron Nashor and the Cloud Dragon both feature in the montage too.
 Blitzcrank gets a moment of his own, with his selection menu cycling between options labeled Volt and God Hand. Neither choice has been explained yet, and Riot has not said how options like these will sit alongside runes.
 Plans for the overhaul first surfaced in a January 2026 entry in Riot’s regular developer updates , where the team said it was building larger, long-term changes to League and ruled out a League of Legends 2. That January roadmap listed a new client tied more closely to the game, a refreshed map, revisions to runes and other picks made before a match, and a better experience for newcomers.
